messages.subject: Creating advanced sleep log
parts:
Hi group,

This may be a silly question but I am trying to wrap my head around the format of the advanced sleep log. I understand you start with a column for date followed by wake time. Does the date correspond to the wake time? And if so, is the onset time the previous night or the night on the date of the wake time.

E.g. Someone falls asleep at 10pm on 2/05/2024, then wakes at 7pm 3/05/2024, and then falls asleep at 11pm on 3/05/2024. Would the sleep diary be formatted like this:

date_d1, wakeup_d1, onset_d1
3/05/2024, 07:00, 23:00

Or would you put the previous night's onset in onset_d1?

Thank you!

Jess

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Creating advanced sleep log
parts:
Hi Jess,

Correct, the advanced sleeplog is date oriented. So, it has the wakeup time and then the bedtime or sleeponset time for the following night. Note this is also the case if the person wakes up after midnight. In your example that would mean that even if the person fell asleep at 1am on 4/5/2024, the sleep diary would still be

date_d1, wakeup_d1, onset_d1
3/05/2024, 07:00, 01:00

Further, you can double check your assumptions by running GGIR and inspecting the guider estimates in the part4_nightsummary_sleep_full.csv because they should reflect the sleep diary for each night.

It would be great if you could suggest how we can improve the phrasing of https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter9_SleepFundamentalsGuiders.html#guider-sleeplog I need to spread my attention to many aspects of GGIR and struggle a bit to optimise every detail, so any feedback will be much appreciated.

Best,

Vincent

On Friday, 9 August 2024 at 2:52 AM, Chong Kar Hau <karh...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Vincent

I also have a question about the use of advanced sleep log. I followed the instructions to create the sleep log file, and I was able to process the data and obtain the sleep results. However, I noticed that the guider estimates in the part4_nightsummary_sleep_full.csv do not match the sleep timings provided in the sleep log file. Below is an example of what I found:

ID night calendar_date guider_inbedStart_ts guider_inbedEnd_ts
Sleep log GGIR Sleep log GGIR
CRO2300012501 (2023-11-27).gt3x 1 26/11/2023 0:00 7:55
CRO2300012501 (2023-11-27).gt3x 2 27/11/2023 22:15 7:00 7:00
CRO2300012501 (2023-11-27).gt3x 3 28/11/2023 22:15 22:30 7:00 7:00
CRO2300012501 (2023-11-27).gt3x 4 29/11/2023 22:30 22:10 7:00 7:00
CRO2300012501 (2023-11-27).gt3x 5 30/11/2023 22:10 22:25 7:00 9:27
CRO2300012501 (2023-11-27).gt3x 6 1/12/2023 22:25 22:30 9:27 9:45
CRO2300012501 (2023-11-27).gt3x 7 2/12/2023 22:30 22:27 9:45 6:50

It appears that GGIR did not match the timing data based on the calendar date but rather according to the number of recording days. For instance, instead of leaving the guider estimates blank for the first two days of recording (which wasn't included in the log diary), it used the data from the subsequent recording days provided in the log diary. Any thoughts/feedback on this would be greatly appreciated.

I have attached the sleep log csv and meta data files for your reference.


Thank you.

Best regards,
John.

Hi Jess,

Correct, the advanced sleeplog is date oriented. So, it has the wakeup time and then the bedtime or sleeponset time for the following night. Note this is also the case if the person wakes up after midnight. In your example that would mean that even if the person fell asleep at 1am on 4/5/2024, the sleep diary would still be

date_d1, wakeup_d1, onset_d1
3/05/2024, 07:00, 01:00

Further, you can double check your assumptions by running GGIR and inspecting the guider estimates in the part4_nightsummary_sleep_full.csv because they should reflect the sleep diary for each night.

It would be great if you could suggest how we can improve the phrasing of https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter9_SleepFundamentalsGuiders.html#guider-sleeplog I need to spread my attention to many aspects of GGIR and struggle a bit to optimise every detail, so any feedback will be much appreciated.
